nodes.title: 1. Dataset Upscale — swap, order, stride and batch sizing, all here
Meta Batch Manager — SET frames_per_batch = frames per view (27 at stride 3)
2. SeedVR2 (7B fp16 @1024 — set batch_size by hand: 5 or 9)
3. Save Upscaled Frames — nothing to configure, it all comes down `job`
Loop driver (throwaway - required by VHS meta-batch)

widgets_values:
WF 2a3 - AS 2a2, BUT ONLY EVERY Nth FRAME

WF1 emits 81 frames per trajectory. That is denser than a splat needs, and every frame
costs a full SeedVR2 pass. select_every_nth on the loader thins it.

THE STRIDE IS APPLIED INSIDE EACH VIEW, NOT ACROSS THE LIST
A plain every-Nth (the kind the VHS loader does) runs over the FLAT sequence. Here that
sequence is camera-major: 24 views x 81 frames (6 cube faces x 4 trajectories). A flat
stride would walk straight through the view boundaries, leaving ragged groups and chunks
holding two different view directions - the one thing the grouping exists to prevent.
This node strides WITHIN each view, so the view COUNT never changes and every chunk stays
inside one view. Counting restarts at each view first frame, so frame 00000 - the real
panorama - is always kept.

EVERYTHING IS ON ONE NODE
The loader does the images -> images_lowres swap (prepare_in_place), resolves the
camera-major order and applies the stride. The saver needs no settings at all: the
target folder, the arrival order and the passthrough list all travel down the single
`job` link. Two SplatKit nodes, one place to configure.

SET frames_per_batch YOURSELF = ONE WHOLE VIEW
The loader prints the number every run ("SET frames_per_batch=27"), and warns if what you
have does not divide the view size - because a chunk spanning two views would hand SeedVR2
two different view directions in one temporal window.

    stride 1 -> 81      stride 3 -> 27      stride 5 -> 17
    stride 2 -> 41      stride 4 -> 21      stride 9 -> 9

(Wiring this automatically is not possible: the manager already feeds the loader, so a link
back would be a dependency cycle - "Dependency cycle detected: 30 -> 10 -> 30".)

SeedVR2 batch_size stays yours too - 5 or 9, whatever fits. Because each iteration is
already inside ONE view, any 4n+1 value up to frames_per_batch is safe; it cannot straddle
a boundary. uniform_batch_size pads the last chunk when it does not divide evenly.

TWO NUMBERS, NOT ONE (this corrects what the 2a2 note said)
frames_per_batch and SeedVR2 batch_size are NOT meant to be equal. The meta-batch gets a
WHOLE view (fewest requeues); SeedVR2 then chunks that view internally with a batch_size
sized to your VRAM.

max_batch_size IS ONLY A VRAM CEILING
batch_size can never exceed the view length, because a chunk larger than the view would
have nothing to fill it. So putting in a number above the view length changes nothing, and
0 means "no ceiling, take the best value". Set it once to the largest batch your card
handles - 9 for 7B fp16 at resolution 1024 - and forget it. The choice is automatic:

    N   frames/view   batch @cap 9   batch uncapped
    1        81             9              81
    2        41             9~             41
    3        27             9               9
    4        21             9~             21
    5        17             9~             17
    9         9             9               9

    ~ = the view does not divide evenly, so the last chunk is short and
        uniform_batch_size pads it (that option is on, and is exactly what it is for).

WHY A RAGGED CHUNK IS FINE NOW
The old "batch_size must divide the view length" rule came from the arrangement where
SeedVR2 was handed the whole concatenated dataset and chunked it from frame 0, blind to
where one view ended and the next began - a non-divisor there meant a chunk containing two
different view directions. Under the Meta Batch Manager it receives exactly ONE view per
call, so every chunk lands inside that view whatever the batch size. Straddling is now
impossible, and divisibility is only about tidiness. The Plan node still prefers an exact
divisor when one fits, and only falls back to a padded tail when the alternative would be
batch_size 1.

drop_partial_stride: 81 at N=5 is 16 complete 5-frame windows plus 1 leftover frame. OFF
keeps it (17/view), ON omits it (16/view). It no longer costs you the batch - 16 and 17
both land on 9 under a cap of 9. N=3 and N=9 divide 81 exactly, so the toggle changes
nothing there. Leave it off unless you specifically want the ragged frame gone.

Strided frames also sit further apart in time, so SeedVR2 has slightly less temporal
correlation to work with between neighbours.

*** THE SKIPPED FRAMES STILL NEED RECONCILING ***
Only the kept frames are written, so images/ ends up thinner than sparse/0/images.bin.
After the run, pick one:

  OPTION 1 - drop them:      python tools\stride_dataset.py <dataset> --every-nth 3 --mode prune --apply
      The skipped frames leave the dataset: images.bin rewritten, their observations
      stripped from points3D.bin, marker sequences filtered. Fewer, uniformly sharp views.
      Undo: python toolsemove_views.py <dataset> --restore

  OPTION 2 - keep them low-res:  ... --every-nth 3 --mode keep-lowres --apply
      The skipped originals are copied back from images_lowres/ and given their OWN camera
      (a clone), so each camera describes exactly one image size. Same view density as
      before, sharp where it counts. Undo: ... stride_dataset.py <dataset> --restore

Both are dry-run by default - run without --apply first to see what would happen. Pass
the SAME --every-nth (and --drop-partial) you used here, or the wrong files get touched.

Everything else - the images -> images_lowres swap, camera-major streaming, writing back
under ORIGINAL filenames, the frame-00000 passthrough - is exactly as in 2a2.

QUICK PREVIEW RECIPE

- camera_index=0 with select_every_nth=9 gives 9 frames of ONE view: a full pass of the
  rail in about a minute, enough to judge resolution / color_correction.
- Then set camera_index=-1 and the N you actually want.
- Console prints every run: the per-view listing, the strided counts, suggested_batch_size,
  and the exact stride_dataset.py command to reconcile afterwards.
- If frames_per_batch does not divide the per-view length the loader warns you rather than
  silently straddling a view.
